english.title: Rape a male under 16
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) raped **(..SPECIFY NAME..), a boy under 16 years.
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) and Schedule 2 of the Sexual Offences Act 1956.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
sexual intercourse per anus
without consent
with a male person
under 16 years of age

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
THIS OFFENCE IS NOW OBSOLETE - now see H5653 or H5669

(i) The definition of rape has been amended to include anal sexual intercourse on a male or female, therefore rape is a more appropriate charge irrespective of the sex of the person involved if consent is absent. (Section 142 Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994).
(ii) As from 1.10.96 conspiring with or inciting another person whilst in the United Kingdom to commit this offence against a child under 16 anywhere in the world is now an offence (the Sexual Offences (Conspiracy and Incitement) Act 1996). See H2007 for the main conspiracy offence.
(iii) See offence wording: H542 - female victim and H558/H559 for rape committed on victims aged 16 or over.
(iv) This offence is included in Schedule 1 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person convicted or cautioned for this offence must comply with the requirements of Section 2 of that Act.
(v) This offence is included in Schedule 2 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person committing this offence outside the United Kingdom may in certain circumstances be prosecuted for that offence in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.
(vi) For the wording of the attempted offence see offence wording H1406.
(vii) IMPORTANT - Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. Provisions under sections 224 to 235 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 may mean that s/he is liable to receive a longer sentence if certain conditions apply.
(viii) Repealed by s.140 of and Schedule 7 to the Sexual Offences Act 2003
